name: Canegauge
description: Hold the reed tube in both hands near the mouth end and feel its balance before loading.

name: Deep Reedtube
description: Pinch a dart by its fletch and slide it into the bore until the tail sits snug.

name: Plugreview
description: Seal the lips around the mouthpiece and draw one slow full breath without shaking the tube.

name: Tubebump
description: Blow one sharp breath through the tube to send the dart straight at a target a few paces off.

name: Square Mouthend
description: Loose dart after dart at a straw post and reset stance and breath after every shot to build steadiness.

name: Huff Skitter
description: Slide one foot sideways while keeping the tube level so aim holds as the body shifts.

name: Pluggauge
description: Draw air low into the belly in three counts to give the next blow more push.

name: Judging Mouthpiece
description: Look down the empty bore at the mark with one eye closed and line the tube on the target.

name: Narrow Hiss
description: Release held air with a snap of the tongue so the dart leaves the bore fast and flat.

name: Tending Plug
description: Pull a cloth through the bore after use so the next dart slides clean and flies true.

name: Deep Airbore
description: Keep the lungs half full while steadying the tube until the sights stop drifting before the shot.

name: Steady Dartfletch
description: Roll a dart across a flat palm to find any bend in the shaft before loading it.

name: Soft Padhead
description: Wrap a tuft of fiber around the dart tail until it fills the bore without sticking.

name: Soft Cane
description: Load from the quiver by feel alone with the thumb on the tail and fingers cupping the point.

name: Narrow Puff
description: Blow a dart at a close target in one clean breath while sighting along the tube.

name: Steady Exhale
description: Load and fire three darts in a row with one steady breath between each to practise rhythm.

name: Backward Tube
description: Kneel on one knee and rest the tube elbow on it to stop the aim from wavering.

name: Gentle Mouthend
description: Draw a fresh dart from a belt quiver without taking the eyes off the mark.

name: Plugamble
description: Place each foot heel first and roll to the toe to close on game without a sound.

name: Watching Cane
description: Stand with held breath and listen for the target to settle before raising the tube.

name: Smooth Tube
description: Raise the tube slowly to the lips on a full held breath so no gasp gives you away.

name: Forward Dartneedle
description: Blow a quick low-pressure puff that sends the dart at near game with barely a hiss.

name: Shifting Huff
description: Press the shoulder to a trunk or wall edge to break the body outline and brace the tube.

name: Quick Needlepuff
description: Blow a second dart on the next breath at the same mark before the target has turned.

name: Tending Mouthpiece
description: Puff the cheeks full and hold the air there to feed a finishing push after the lungs spend.

name: Reedtube Gauge
description: Sweep air in from the bottom of the lungs to the top in one long slow pull.

name: Measured Airbore
description: Keep the chest raised and still while counting beats so the tube does not bob.

name: Square Plug
description: Collapse the cheeks sharply after the lung blow to add speed to the dart at mid range.

name: Hissstrike
description: Spend one full lungful in a single sustained blow to carry the dart as far as the tube allows.

name: Tubereview
description: Breathe out and in twice through the nose to clear the burn between volleys.

name: Huffblow
description: Fire a dart at each rung of a ladder of marks and adjust the blow for every distance.

name: Canecowl
description: Swat a thrown object aside with the tube held crosswise when the lungs are empty.

name: Canecount
description: Trim the fiber tail of a dart with a small knife until it seats snug in the bore.

name: Tubegauge
description: Twist a leaf vane onto the shaft so the dart spins and holds a straight course.

name: Watching Dartfletch
description: Test the dart on a fingertip to find its balance point and shift the tip weight to suit.

name: Tubedash
description: Blow a spin-fletched dart along a straight line with a little qi easing the breath.

name: Leaden Burst
description: Shoot two differently fletched darts at one distance and compare how each falls.

name: Deep Cane
description: Seat the lips on the rim of the mouthpiece so no air leaks round the edge.

name: Warm Mouthpiece
description: Bring the dominant eye in line with the bore and the mark until all three agree.

name: Watching Padhead
description: Lay the leading finger along the tube's upper side to guide the muzzle.

name: Flat Burst
description: Blow a dart at a small mark within a few strides so it strikes exactly where the bore points.

name: Solid Tube
description: Thrust the loaded tube out at arm's length to fend off a grab while the dart stays seated.

name: Sideways Hiss
description: Take a quarter step and swing the muzzle onto a second mark without lowering the tube.

name: Stopping Needlepuff
description: Blow a loud sharp puff with no dart to startle an animal or foe into pausing.

name: Judging Padhead
description: Blow across the mouthpiece to sound a short note that shows how the air runs through the bore.

name: Puffdrop
description: Blow a pinch of fine grit through the tube into the eyes of a close foe.

name: Exhaledrop
description: Blow a light blunt dart to sting bare skin and warn a target away rather than wound it.

name: Burstblow
description: Back away while blowing quick darts to keep a pursuer's head down.

name: Fouling Exhale
description: Level the loaded tube at a foe and hold a firm stare to make them stop where they stand.

name: Warm Dartneedle
description: Listen for where a warning dart lands to judge the distance to a hidden target.

name: Even Mouthend
description: Twist two tube sections together until the bore runs smooth with no step at the join.

name: Shifting Exhale
description: Sling the separate sections across the back so they ride quietly while walking.

name: Smooth Airbore
description: Assemble the tube from its pieces in a slow practised count while watching the target.

name: Gentle Dartfletch
description: Blow once through the new joint to feel for any leak at the seam.

name: Flat Hiss
description: Fire from the full-length jointed tube for the longer steadier flight its length gives.

name: Plugcount
description: Draw a thread of qi down with the breath and hold it low behind the navel.

name: Square Needlepuff
description: Push the held qi up behind a blow so the dart flies faster than breath alone allows.

name: Smooth Reedtube
description: Feel the qi thin out along the exhale and keep it level to the last of the breath.

name: Even Plug
description: Spread a faint layer of qi over the dart tip before loading so it bites cleaner.

name: Pufftrot
description: Step forward on the in-breath so the qi gathers as the body settles for the shot.

name: Huffdash
description: Open the throat suddenly to free the stored qi in one burst behind a dart.
